components.name: Evidence label
components.description: A compact label that makes source provenance or state easy to scan.

narrative.overview: Kelus should feel like a precise study notebook that can answer for itself. It is editorial rather than decorative: calm paper, deep ink, visible source evidence, and a single green signal when the learner has a clear next move. Marketing makes the promise tangible with real product fragments; the product makes each decision traceable to a student’s own notes.
keyCharacteristics: Editorial type paired with fast, legible interface text.
Paper-and-ink surfaces with one deliberate green action per decision.
Real source evidence and product output instead of decorative mock-ups.
Motion that confirms a change, then gets out of the way.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Use green for the current action or current route. If every surface becomes green, the learner loses the one thing to do next.

rules.name: The Reading-First Rule
rules.body: Use the serif only when a student is reading a lesson, a topic, or a meaningful outcome. Keep operational UI in Inter.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Never add a shadow merely to make a component look clickable. Use a fill, border, and interaction state instead.

dos: Do show the original line, page, or section beside an answer whenever Kelus makes a judgment.
Do let whitespace and hairlines create order before reaching for a container.
Do keep one primary action per decision and make its wording say what happens next.
Do make motion explain a result, finish within 80–400ms, and honor reduced-motion preferences.
Do use the Notion-style illustration pack only as a human counterweight to real product evidence.
donts: Don't use generic SaaS cards, blue glows, stock art, or generated illustrations.
Don't use a decorative color as a button fill or mix source, recall, and route colors without their study meaning.
Don't add a card inside a card, a shadow stack, or a second primary action merely to fill space.
Don't animate headings or body copy, loop demonstrations, or make product controls bounce.
Don't use the marketing serif for dense practice controls or call a topic a concept, section, or idea.
